common.applies_to: Established bush rose (Hybrid Tea, Floribunda, provisional Grandiflora); dormant pruning
common.preserved_uncertainty: Causes aren't equally evidenced: sunscald rests on one source, and rodent and snow damage on one each (AF-2). Signs of physical damage are visible ones only (AF-6, as corrected 17 October 2026). The borer entry hole and the harmless-wasp caveat rest on one page each and are not shown (AF-7). Experts disagree on whether canker can be diagnosed from a photo (C-3), so Pip always states its confidence. Sources are UK, US and Australian.

content.look_for: Now let's look for damaged growth — canes that are injured or diseased.

criteria.text: Canker: brown to purplish sunken patches with cracking edges, tiny black dots, or dieback above a patch that rings the cane.
Frost or winter injury: browned shoot tips and discoloured canes. Cutting into a cane shows the pith (its centre), and the pith's colour tells living wood from dead.
Physical damage: a broken cane, or damage where canes rub together.
Borer (an insect that tunnels into canes): a new shoot tip that suddenly wilts, or a swollen spot on the cane.
criteria.limit: A wilting tip can have other causes.

criteria.text: Not damage: mossy or spiny galls on canes are generally harmless.
criteria.limit: One source says a heavy infestation of mossy gall can weaken the plant above it.

content.photo_limit: A photo can show outside signs, but not what's happening inside the cane.
content.confirm_question: Find that cane on your rose. Can you see damage like this?
content.not_sure_guidance: Look closely at that spot on the plant itself, not at a photo.
content.any_more_question: Can you see any more damaged stems?
